messages:
Maya: Heads-up — ran a 2hr synthetic surge sim for EU night window (model: redwood-30b-q4f16, seq=1024, mix of sync/streaming calls). Results look tighter than expected. p99 latencies spike at ~2.8s when concurrency hits 210 on A100 pool.

Oliver: Oof. Is that with current batching and KV cache enabled?

Maya: Yes. Batching=auto, KV cache warm for 80% of prefixes. Kernel mix: 60% fast-matmul, 40% fallback micro-kernel due to long sequences.

Sasha: Can you paste the short table you used? That p99 number sounds like concurrency headroom issue + warmup tail.

Maya: Sure — pasted from the sim CSV: ```
region, gpu_type, pool_size, concurrency_target, p50_lat_ms, p95_lat_ms, p99_lat_ms, tpm
EU, A100-40G, 30, 180, 210, 870, 2800, 4200
EU, A100-40G, 30, 210, 240, 1100, 2800, 4900
EU, H100-80G, 18, 210, 190, 720, 1200, 5100
US, A100-40G, 30, 210, 220, 900, 2600, 4800
```
(note: tpm = tokens per minute equivalent workload)

Ricardo: Interesting that H100 p99 is lower for same concurrency but tpm similar. Are kernels on H100 picking newer fused attention kernels?

Maya: Yep — H100 run used kernel set v3.4 with fused attention + int8 matmul path for q4f16, which shaved p99 by ~40%.

Emma: For Dedicated capacity sizing we should aim for a safety factor. Our standard is 1.5x peak observed, but for EU night pockets maybe 1.8x given tail sensitivity.

Oliver: How does autoscaler react? If we target concurrency_target=150 per GPU vs 210, what's the pool delta?

Maya: Quick notes from sim: at target 150 (A100) pool of 30 -> effective headroom for 2x surge is marginal. To keep p99 < 1200ms during 2x median surge we'd need ~40 A100s or switch 12 of them to H100s (heterogeneous pool) and keep pool at 30.

Sasha: Heterogeneous pool sounds appealing but adds routing complexity. Do we have fallback policy if H100 capacity drops?

Maya: Yes — smart routing will fall back to A100 with degraded latency and our canary policy triggers route-splitting at 5% error/latency drift.

InfraBot: Autoscale event recorded: simulated scale from 30 -> 41 A100s over 95s in the stress run (policy: cpu+latency composite).

Ricardo: Cost ballpark? 40 A100s vs 30 with 12 H100 replacements — what's delta?

Maya: Monthlyized roughs: 40xA100 = +~30% infra cost vs baseline 30 A100s. 18A100+12H100 hetero ~~ +18% but H100 hourly is pricier per-GPU; depends on instance sizing and reserved pricing.

Emma: Recommendation: for EU night window we propose a short-term plan: 1) Add +10 A100s as buffer for Q2 launch, 2) run pilot of 6 H100s in the pool and shift 20% of high-priority routes to them, 3) tighten autoscaler latency threshold to trigger earlier.

Oliver: +1 to the cautious approach. Also suggest we tweak batching policy to prefer smaller batch cutover at >150ms queueing to reduce p99 tails.

Sasha: Agree. I'll open a quick PR to change batch_cutover_ms from 200 -> 150 for dedicated pools in EU night window.

Maya: Thanks. I'll export the full sim logs and attach to the capacity runbook. Quick note: observed perf cliff when mixture of streaming and sync causes an unexpected head-of-line blocking — worth adding a test lane.

Emma: Can you add a short checklist item: "validate no head-of-line blocking with mixed streaming + sync at concurrency 200" to the runbook?

Maya: Done — added. Also flagged for model-onboarding that q4f16 is borderline for some long-form prompts; may need re-run with q5-fast variant for those customers.

Ricardo: Let's revisit after Sasha's batching tweak and Maya's pilot H100 numbers. If p99 improves < 1.2s at concurrency 200 we can defer larger pool buys.

Oliver: Cool. Who's owning the cost calc for the hetero option?

Ricardo: I'll take cost calc and ROI for hetero pool. ETA EOD tomorrow.

Maya: I'll drop sim artifacts + runbook link here when ready. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
